runners_data.name: Harbour Vision
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old carrying big weight who fades in the finish at 7f-8f, genuinely a hold-up type pushed into midfield representation — at 1m½f this is a longer trip and the modest pace won't help her late effort; jockey Frederick Tett has had just 1 winner from 23 rides for Scott Dixon in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Silky Lass
runners_data.note: Three-year-old in decent recent form (1-3-3 in last five) who handles Standard AW well and was placed at Wolverhampton last time; a natural hold-up filly who needs a decent pace to get into the race, which is the key risk here.

runners_data.name: Pentonville
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old who has placed twice over this distance in similar company but nearly all her form comes on Good ground rather than Standard, making the AW surface a mild concern; trainer Boughey has had no winners from 20 runners in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Quick Quasar
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and likely sole front-runner; returns from a 78-day absence which is a flag, but her two most recent runs on Standard going show a win and a place over 7f, and stepping up to 1m½f as the uncontested leader could suit her stamina profile if she settles.

runners_data.name: Rhythm N Rock
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with 15 from 15 runs on Standard going and a recent Wolverhampton AW win; hold-up style means a strong pace would help, but his class at this level and course familiarity make him competitive even if the pace is modest — T14 of 3/26 is solid.

runners_data.name: Imola
runners_data.note: The most interesting prominent racer in the field with six runs showing 3 wins and consistent place finishes on Standard AW; trainer Joey Ramsden has had no winners from 11 runs in 14 days, but Imola's own form record is strong and the trip and surface are squarely in her wheelhouse.

runners_data.name: Volto Di Medusa
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won last time at Wolverhampton AW over 8f on Standard going but much of her recent form comes on Good, making this surface record mixed; the step up in trip is likely fine, though the modest pace is a hurdle for her get-off-the-bridle style.

runners_data.name: Sandret
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old genuine hold-up horse returning from 291 days off — the layoff is a significant concern regardless of ability; mapped into midfield rather than the rear where he naturally operates, and his best form has come on Good ground rather than Standard AW.

runners_data.name: Molly Valentine
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (0-7-0-7-0 last five runs) suggests she is struggling for confidence; a natural hold-up mare mapped forward out of necessity, carrying a hood, and her trainer Stephanie Cassidy has had zero runners in the last 14 days — hard to find a case for her.

runners_data.name: Ebn Sabt
runners_data.note: Three-year-old returning quickly (10 days) after two disappointing AW runs; wears a hood, genuine hold-up type who is mapped into midfield, and his only win came at 8f on Standard going — the trip extension to 1m½f is unproven and the pace shape doesn't assist him.

runners_data.name: Hashtagnotions
runners_data.note: A prominent racer by style who wears a hood and has struggled to win — zero wins from 15 starts — but has placed three times and ran a solid 3rd at 10f on Standard last time; Richard and Peter Fahey's 14-day record of 5 wins from 57 runners gives some trainer momentum and the trip should suit.

runners_data.name: Pipily
runners_data.note: Three-year-old back after 318 days off, all three prior runs came on Soft or Good ground rather than Standard AW, and the trip is unproven beyond 7f; a hold-up type pushed into midfield, the lengthy absence and unknown AW profile make it very difficult to assess her chance.

runners_data.name: This Rib
runners_data.note: Unknown style runner with a pull-up in recent form and all her runs limited to 7f on varying ground — the step up to 1m½f is a significant unknown; trainer Loughnane has a 3/21 14-day record but this filly's form string and trip inexperience are major question marks.

races.paceDynamic: Quick Quasar is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field over 1m½f on Wolverhampton's All-Weather, and with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead, she can dictate an unhurried, controlled gallop from the front. Imola and Hashtagnotions are the natural prominent horses who will look to sit just behind her, creating a sustainable tempo rather than a pressured one — the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. With no one to force Quick Quasar off a comfortable lead, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently and quicken into the straight, rather than deep closers who depend on a strong pace being set. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Harbour Vision, Sandret, Molly Valentine, Ebn Sabt, and Pipily are all true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map, and of those, Sandret and Harbour Vision are the most likely to actually operate furthest back, though even they will find the pace shape working against them.

scenarios.body: If Imola or a prominent rival pushes up early and forces a genuinely stronger gallop, opening the race up for hold-up horses.

scenarios.body: If the field concertinas badly in a slowly-run race and redistributed hold-up horses find gaps late to produce a late flourish.

watchPoints.text: Quick Quasar's 78-day absence is the single biggest risk to Scenario A — watch if she travels smoothly in the early stages or shows signs of ring rust, as an unfit leader could be caught late.

Imola is likely to press Quick Quasar hardest from a prominent pitch — if she sits upsides or forces the pace rather than tracking, the race tempo could shift dramatically and open the door for hold-up horses.

Sandret and Harbour Vision — both genuine hold-up types mapped forward out of necessity — should be watched for whether they are restrained to their natural deep position or pushed up; if they are covered up, they will need a pace that this race shape is unlikely to provide.

Several hold-up horses in this field are carrying big weights (Rhythm N Rock 156lbs, Imola 152lbs, Volto Di Medusa 151lbs) — watch whether the amateur jockeys judge the pace correctly at the top of the weight range, as errors in judgment could create false early fractions.

Pipily and Sandret both return from layoffs exceeding 300 days — watch their behaviour in the pre-race and early stages, as ring rustiness from either could cause interference or positional disruption in a 13-runner field.

runners_data.name: Enter Sandman
runners_data.note: Decent recent form including wins at Wolverhampton at 6f on Standard, and the headgear (tongue-tie, cheekpieces) points to a horse who needs galvanising — Richard Spencer's yard is in solid form at T14 6/16, and this runner's hold-up style means it needs at least a competent gallop to land its finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Standard ground last time out and the form is directly relevant, though the blinkered headgear and Dylan Hogan booking suggest connections want a positive ride; a hold-up horse by nature who needs to hold his recent improvement.

runners_data.name: Go Lockers Go
runners_data.note: Two wins in recent form including a 6f Wolverhampton Standard victory, and Daniel Muscutt's booking adds confidence — a genuine hold-up type who nevertheless has the profile to travel into contention mid-race if the pace is moderate.

runners_data.name: She's Divine
runners_data.note: The lone prominent-style runner outside Guernsey Angel, and her three consecutive placed efforts over 5-6f on Standard suggest she handles this surface well; 161 days off is a concern and Mark Loughnane has had no winners in 18 runners at T14, dimming her claims despite the ideal tactical position.

runners_data.name: Tie Fighter
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's runner wears blinkers and ran with credit when second over 5f on Soft — a natural hold-up horse whose chances here are tempered by being displaced from his preferred rear position into a midfield slot that doesn't suit his style in a moderate-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Victor Cee
runners_data.note: Has shown ability when placed at 6f on Standard and soft ground, but Connor Planas takes the ride on a horse whose natural instinct is to come from the back — condensed into a midfield berth by the volume of rear-runners in this field, his role asks him to race positionally forward of his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Goldenstateofmind
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell picks up the ride on a horse who has struggled to improve past a 7th placing on Standard ground recently — a true hold-up runner squeezed into a midfield slot by the field's composition, and the blinkered headgear has not yet unlocked improvement.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: One win in the form string (Goodwood, 6f) but recent efforts are poor, and Jack Callan's claim is noted; a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield because this field cannot accommodate the volume of true rear-runners, and the long absence from winning form compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Nzuri
runners_data.note: Has a notable tendency to fade in the finish which is a significant red flag in any scenario — Jack Channon's yard is active at T14 (3/14), but this hold-up type's pattern of weakening late means even a good tactical position may not translate into a finish, and the 29-day break adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon runner with cheekpieces (hg:v) who has shown early pace before but recorded modest AW figures — a hold-up horse displaced into midfield by field composition, and the best recent effort of 4th on Soft rather than Standard limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Filly Foden
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's runner has placed at 3rd over 6f Standard in recent form and Lewis Edmunds takes the ride — a hold-up type who appears in midfield on the map but whose natural rhythm is from the back, and the form string shows more placed efforts than many rivals which keeps her interesting.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner and Pat Cosgrave's booking at OR 69 is respected — Style Fit of 0.92 is a minor flag, but no horse in this field looks likely to push her early, and her ability to control fractions from the front without being pressured makes her the central shape-setter in this race.

runners_data.name: Escape Plan
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner and takes no further part in the analysis.

races.paceDynamic: Guernsey Angel is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — She's Divine is the only other prominent-style runner and is unlikely to push hard enough to turn this into a true test of pace. With Guernsey Angel able to dictate at a comfortable, controlled tempo on Standard Wolverhampton ground, this shapes as a slowly-run-on-paper sprint where the fractions will not be truly searching, compressing the finishing kick of genuine hold-up horses. The field is overloaded with natural rear-of-field types — Victor Cee, Tie Fighter, King Of Chaos, Goldenstateofmind, Nzuri, Beach Partee and Filly Foden are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots because they simply cannot all settle at the back — meaning those shown in midfield on the map are racing out of their natural role rather than expressing genuine positional preference. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can race prominently or make ground from the middle of the pack without needing a truly strong gallop to stretch the field — closers who need a genuine burning pace to set up their finishing kick are at a structural disadvantage here.

watchPoints.text: Guernsey Angel breaks cleanly and Pat Cosgrave pushes forward — if she crosses to the rail and sets an uncontested lead through the first furlong, the race shape is effectively locked in from that point.

She's Divine is 161 days absent and faces a steep ask on fitness grounds — watch how she travels through the first three furlongs; if she struggles to hold her prominent position, the front-running scenario becomes even more one-dimensional.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Victor Cee, King Of Chaos, Goldenstateofmind — may all break forward simultaneously in search of position, creating a brief scramble for midfield spots in the opening furlong that could disrupt runners tracking them.

Go Lockers Go's two recent wins both came at 5f — stepping back up to 6f at Wolverhampton on Standard is familiar but watch whether Daniel Muscutt rides her prominently or patiently, as that decision will determine whether she gets into contention before or after the bend.

Nzuri's flagged tendency to fade in the finish means backers should watch her early position — if she is travelling well into the final two furlongs but then weakens, it confirms the pattern and signals the race is going to a horse with better finishing resolution.

runners_data.name: Bumaan
runners_data.note: A progressive 3yo for George Boughey who arrives 69 days fresh, with three Standard-going runs all producing placed finishes (sim-going 3/3); the step up to 1m4f is a new challenge and Jack Callan's 3lb claim could offset any conditional inexperience — natural hold-up style suits this shape.

runners_data.name: Al Amirah
runners_data.note: Has six runs on Standard going with no wins or places, but the step to 1m4f today is the furthest she has tried and Ismail Mohammed's yard is in quiet form (0/1 T14); Mason Paetel's 5lb claim adds appeal but her entire profile screams that the trip could unlock latent stamina.

runners_data.name: Mick The Hat
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's yard is firing well (9/44 T14) and this 3yo returns quickly after 12 days, landing a pleasing third over 1m4f on Soft last time; only 2/4 on Standard so the surface is a minor query, but the trip confirmation and powerful trainer form make him one of the more interesting runners.

runners_data.name: Last Flight
runners_data.note: James Ferguson sends this one out in fair form (3/10 T14) and Last Flight has three consecutive seventh-place finishes, including two at this trip on Standard — a true hold-up horse whose natural style is to race from the rear, though in a field of closers he cannot get the detached position he ideally needs, tempering his chance.

runners_data.name: Ethereal Charm
runners_data.note: Daisy Hitchins' runner carries a modest record (0/5 T14) and the form string shows a concerning 0 last time out; on her best day she has placed at 8f but this 10f test in an all-closer field means she is operating out of her comfort zone positionally, with her staying credentials on Standard still untested beyond 7f.

runners_data.name: Keep It Classic
runners_data.note: William Haggas (6/29 T14) is in fair form and this horse has a useful second over 1m4f at Goodwood in the book, though notably flagged as prone to fading in the finish — on a Standard surface over this trip with no front-runner to chase, that fade tendency is an obvious risk even though the trainer angle is attractive.

runners_data.name: Ada Rose
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's runner has one win and one place in five Standard-going starts and was a placed third over 1m4f on Standard recently — Jack Mitchell is a capable claimer and the combination of trip confirmation and AW familiarity makes this one worth noting, though she has been out-classed at this level before.

runners_data.name: Risk Averse Rebel
runners_data.note: Three placed efforts in her last five runs, all on Standard going, and a recent third at 1m4f on Standard is directly relevant form; Gary Hanmer's yard has no recent winners (0/8 T14) but the horse herself looks the most consistently form-consistent runner in this field and her stamina at the trip is proven.

runners_data.name: Panthere Noir
runners_data.note: Luke Dace's 3yo has one Standard-going place from 13 attempts on the surface, which is a sobering statistic; a 7lb claimer in Jude Fernandes rides and the horse has shown up over 1m4f on Good ground, but the AW record is thin and this field asks questions the form does not confidently answer.

runners_data.name: Lady Lauren
runners_data.note: William Cox rides for Ed de Giles whose yard is quiet (0/7 T14); Lady Lauren has placed figures on Good-ish and Soft ground at shorter trips but steps up sharply to 1m4f on Standard for the first time — her form is mostly over 8f and the combination of unfamiliar trip, AW surface, and out-of-form yard makes this a speculative entry.

races.paceDynamic: Wolverhampton's 1m4f on the all-weather at Standard going favours a truly-run affair, yet this field contains no confirmed front-runner — every single runner is catalogued as a hold-up type, meaning the race will almost certainly begin at a crawl before developing into a late sprint-finish test of raw ability over the closing stages. With no horse willing to take the race by the scruff from flag-fall, the early tempo is likely to be pedestrian, bunching the field and placing maximum emphasis on finishing kick inside the final two furlongs. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Last Flight, Keep It Classic, Ethereal Charm, Ada Rose, Risk Averse Rebel, Panthere Noir and Lady Lauren are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield simply because they cannot all trail the field simultaneously. Given a pace vacuum and a bunch finish, the runners who combine the best current form, most relevant experience at this trip on the all-weather, and the most forceful jockey booking will hold the clearest tactical edge — this race shape favours hold-up types with strong finishing form who can accelerate from a position just off the non-existent pace, particularly those with proven Standard-going stamina at 1m2f-plus.

watchPoints.text: Risk Averse Rebel is the form horse of the race with three places in five Standard-going runs including a recent third at 1m4f on Standard — watch for Gina Mangan to place her prominently from a hold-up position and deliver the most reliable finishing effort in this field.

Keep It Classic is trained by the in-form William Haggas and has placed over 1m4f but is specifically flagged as prone to fading in the finish — if the pace quickens sharply in the final furlong, watch for this one to get caught late despite travelling well two furlongs out.

With no confirmed front-runner, watch for a false or dawdling pace in the opening mile — any horse whose jockey panics and goes too early from the hold-up pack could end up running into a wall of tired horses in the straight rather than finding clear running.

Mick The Hat's trainer Ralph Beckett is significantly in form (9/44 T14) and the horse confirmed he stays 1m4f with a third on Soft last time — watch whether Jack Dace attempts to use that stamina advantage by racing more prominently than his hold-up label suggests.

Ada Rose holds a placed effort at 1m4f on Standard and Jack Mitchell is an accomplished rider — watch whether he exploits the pace vacuum by positioning more positively than the hold-up tag implies, potentially stealing a march on rivals who are all waiting for each other.

runners_data.name: Saturnalia
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with 0W3P in similar going from five comparable starts; finishing positions of 4th and 8th recently suggest a placed threat rather than a winner, but the J S Moore yard is 0/20 in the past 14 days which tempers confidence sharply.

runners_data.name: Taskheer
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and only confirmed pace-setter in the field; 1W7P in similar going from 13 visits is solid, though STYLE_FIT at 0.93 is flagged because this trip and field size may push her slightly out of comfort zone — still the key tactical horse.

runners_data.name: Vecchio
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose true style is rear-of-field, pushed into a midfield mapping simply because the field is over-stocked with closers; Scott Dixon has 1 winner from 23 in the past fortnight and the 0W0P from comparable history is concerning.

runners_data.name: Rockafeller Skank
runners_data.note: A three-year-old whose last two wins came on soft ground at 8-10f, so the switch to AW Standard is an unproven query; true hold-up style means the track conditions and redistribution to midfield both work against a natural running pattern.

runners_data.name: Arlecchino's Rex
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with 1W7P from 15 similar-going starts and a strong record at 10f on AW — the headgear (h) and Daniel Muscutt booking give this runner a positive profile, and proven ability to finish close in this trip and going makes it a key player.

runners_data.name: First Encounter
runners_data.note: Holds two wins from eight AW starts at this distance and going combination, making the course-and-distance form here the most compelling in the field; the 14-day absence is fine and the b headgear has previously been worn in winning runs.

runners_data.name: Manton Road
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse that has been redistributed to midfield; only 1W2P from 8 comparable starts and recent form readings of 6-5770 make this one hard to enthuse about, with the AW going conversion rate moderate at best.

runners_data.name: Gloriola
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying 124lbs for Steph Hollinshead, absent 51 days and with no AW or standard-going form to speak of in five career runs — the form string 680-05 reads poorly and the layoff adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Smoker Bellamy
runners_data.note: A three-year-old whose best effort was 2nd over 10f on Standard going, giving it the stamina angle for this trip; however, genuine hold-up style mapped to midfield due to field congestion, and only 0W1P from 2 similar-going efforts limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Sorted
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 8f on Standard AW and ran 3rd last time, so there is form to build on at 84 days off; the redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up position means the steady pace set by Taskheer may not generate the late burst this style needs.

runners_data.name: Thomas Tallis
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with 0W0P from four runs and a form string of 870-7 that inspires little; 14 days since last run and no placings on Standard going — best viewed as an each-way longshot only if the race falls apart completely.

runners_data.name: Rogue Soldier
runners_data.note: Absent 145 days, which is the longest layoff in the field, and a form string of 409-00 suggests deteriorating form; despite 2W4P from 13 similar-going starts historically, the extended absence and recent blanks make this very hard to trust.

races.paceDynamic: Taskheer is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, should stride away from the gates and control the pace entirely at her own leisure over 1m½f on Wolverhampton's standard Polytrack. With one horse setting an uncontested, sustainable tempo over this stamina-testing trip, the race is likely to develop into a steady-run affair with a single sustained effort from the front rather than a sprint finish off a scorching pace. The heavy redistribution in this field is telling — Sorted, Manton Road, Smoker Bellamy, Rogue Soldier, Thomas Tallis, Vecchio and Rockafeller Skank are all mapped out of their natural positions because there are simply too many hold-up horses to occupy the rear; the horses most likely to actually secure prominent tracking positions behind Taskheer are those with the highest gate agility or forward tendency, but with STYLE_FIT discounts across the board, most will end up bunched in a pack mid-to-rear. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently in second or third off the controlled pace and sustain their effort into the straight, or those with strong proven form at this exact track and trip who can deliver a clean late run — not true hold-up types who need a genuine breakneck gallop to generate momentum.

watchPoints.text: Taskheer controls the entire tempo — watch whether Ashley Lewis (5) settles her kindly or allows her to bowl along too freely, as any sustained strong pace from the front risks burning out over 1m½f with 12 runners behind.

Arlecchino's Rex has Daniel Muscutt aboard and holds the strongest AW similar-going profile among the hold-up horses — watch its position at the turn for home as the horse most likely to capitalise on the controlled pace with a clean run.
First Encounter's two AW wins at this course and distance make it a serious watch if it can secure a prominent position early, though the field congestion means a clean passage is not guaranteed.

Rogue Soldier's 145-day absence combined with declining recent form (409-00) means it should be monitored for signs of ring-rustiness — a non-runner or poor show here would confirm its current rating is flattering.

The sheer volume of redistributed horses (seven runners) means the straight could produce a bunched finish — watch for signs of trouble in running as horses switch lines late in a congested midfield pack.

races.name: Book To Stay At Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sheik Yerbouti
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Grace Harris whose form figures of 8/11 show limited recent impact, and a flagged tendency to fade in the finish makes this flat, straight 5f particularly unforgiving — needs a strong pace collapse that is unlikely to materialise here.

runners_data.name: Argy Bhaji
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's consistent performer has placed in five of his last five starts, all at 6f, and drops to 5f here for the first time — the shorter trip is an unknown, but his prominent style suits the pace map and Muscutt is a strong booking.

runners_data.name: Project Wallace
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just a single run to his name (fourth over 5f on Standard), the Declan Carroll runner has shown enough at this trip to be interesting but his style is unclassified and his chance hinges on unexposed potential.

runners_data.name: Roy Lane
runners_data.note: K R Burke's gelding arrives after 53 days off the track with modest form figures of 13 and 6 on different going, and the hold-up style suits him poorly over this flat, uncontested 5f sprint where there is little expectation of a late pace collapse.

runners_data.name: Spaceman
runners_data.note: The Richard & Peter Fahey runner is the confirmed pacesetter here, and while the STYLE_FIT flag notes he may be racing out of role relative to his best efforts, this uncontested lead on flat Wolverhampton AW is the most favourable scenario his profile will encounter in this field.

runners_data.name: Baby G
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's debutant carries an unknown going profile and unknown style — an X-factor runner who could perform well fresh or miss the mark entirely; Carroll's trainer-14-day strike rate of 10/58 suggests reasonable yard form.

runners_data.name: Good Guys Girl
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado saddles this unexposed three-year-old on debut with going profile unknown and style unclassified; Sean Bowen takes the ride, providing experience in the plate, but without form to anchor expectations she is a speculative runner.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Melody
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's filly finished fifth over 6f at Goodwood on her sole start and is a genuine hold-up type by nature — she has been mapped to midfield as the field is stacked with similar profiles, but her actual racing position will likely be towards the rear, making a 5f straight sprint a tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Spaceman is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on a flat 5f Wolverhampton AW straight, will likely bowl along at a sustainable but uncontested gallop from the outset, setting a controlled pace with no rival capable of matching him stride-for-stride from the gates. Argy Bhaji will press forward from a prominent position and may apply some early pressure, but with no other natural leader in the field, the pace shape is unlikely to be truly searching. Hold-up runners Sheik Yerbouti, Roy Lane, and the redistributed Moonlight Melody will need the tempo to lift in the final two furlongs to deliver their challenges from off the pace, but on a flat, straight 5f track against an uncontested leader, that acceleration may arrive too late. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-leading types who can control position early and sustain their effort to the line — the lack of genuine pace pressure plays directly into Spaceman's hands and those who can race just behind him. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their natural positions; Spaceman is best placed to lead, with Argy Bhaji most likely to lock in a front-rank berth, while Moonlight Melody — a true hold-up type — has been mapped to midfield but is unlikely to be travelling in that position naturally.

watchPoints.text: Spaceman gets a clean break — if Oisin Orr slots him across to the rail unchallenged in the first two strides, the uncontested lead over this flat 5f track makes him extremely difficult to reel in.

Argy Bhaji's jockey Daniel Muscutt may attempt to push up and pressurise Spaceman early — any sustained duel between the two in the first furlong would meaningfully increase the chance of a closer finishing over the top of both.

Baby G and Good Guys Girl are both debutants with unknown style profiles — either could break sharply and steal a prominent position, altering the pace map entirely before the first furlong is complete.

Roy Lane's 53-day absence and hold-up style over a flat 5f track represent a significant double concern — watch whether Pierre-Louis Jamin elects to ride him more prominently than his natural style to compensate for the trip.

Moonlight Melody's redistribution to midfield masks a true hold-up profile — Callum Hutchinson will almost certainly be further back than the map suggests, and any ground lost in positioning on this sharp 5f trip is unlikely to be recovered.

races.name: Cavani Modern Gentleman Handicap

runners_data.name: Kaaranah
runners_data.note: Solid recent form including two wins over this course and distance on Standard going (sim-going 2W4P) makes the trip and surface no concern, though as a true hold-up performer, Jack Callan on a 3-claim will need to judge the pace carefully if this horse finds itself shuffled closer than ideal.

runners_data.name: Study Up
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and key pace-setter for the entire field; Jonny Peate will look to dictate from the front with no pressure expected, and the tongue-tie is worn again — this horse must be respected as the race-shaper even if its style-fit score reflects a slight step up in role.

runners_data.name: Beachborough Girl
runners_data.note: Trainer Julia & Shelley Birkett in fine 14-day form (3/11), and Beachborough Girl has strong course-and-distance form on Standard going (sim-going 2W7P, 11/15 runs); a genuine hold-up horse whose true finishing kick may be compromised if she cannot get back from the pace-compressed midfield her redistribution places her in.

runners_data.name: Wolf Of Badenoch
runners_data.note: Poor sim-going figures (0W0P, 4/15) on Standard surfaces are a real concern, and the 27-day absence adds to the query; despite being a natural hold-up type, he is likely to find himself closer to the pace than he wants in this shape, which does little to offset the going doubts.

runners_data.name: Eagle Day
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant red flag when Study Up is likely to set a comfortable, front-running tempo — Pat Cosgrave on a horse with a stamina fade profile over 1m1½f on AW at Wolverhampton needs the pace to be genuinely strong, which it is unlikely to be here.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell takes over on a horse that has headgear noted and whose sim-going figures show limited positives (0W2P); a hold-up horse stepping back slightly in trip from 1m2f runs, and the moderate pace is unlikely to suit a horse that needs others to tire in front.

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Daniel Muscutt is a strong booking and this 8-year-old has strong sim-going form (0W5P, 13/15), suggesting he handles the surface and trips well; he has been racing over longer distances recently and the drop to 1m1½f could be a slight question, though he is consistent enough to be competitive if he travels.

runners_data.name: Asian Journey
runners_data.note: Sam England's yard is in excellent 14-day form (5/15) and Asian Journey has won on Standard going over 8f, but the step up to 1m1½f is untested in recent history — a true hold-up type placed in midfield on the map, he will need the pace to lift turning for home.

runners_data.name: Implied Volatility
runners_data.note: A 151-day absence is a major concern, and the form string (0477-7) shows no recent encouragement; a hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution, the long layoff on top of modest exposed form makes this a very difficult proposition regardless of race shape.

runners_data.name: Le Pelerin
runners_data.note: William Knight's yard is active (3/17 in 14 days) and Marco Ghiani is a capable claimer, but Le Pelerin's form figures show consistent midfield and rear finishes on a variety of surfaces; the horse's true hold-up style will be pushed forward by the map position, which is likely to be against his preferences.

runners_data.name: Have You A Minute
runners_data.note: A 197-day absence is the dominant concern here, and while Sean Bowen is an experienced rider who can coax a first run out of a returning horse, the form prior to the break was mixed (2W4P in sim-going but finishing 11th and 6th last two runs on Standard); the hold-up style redistributed to midfield adds further complication on reappearance.

races.paceDynamic: Study Up is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this 11-runner field, will dictate from the front at a sustainable, controlled tempo over the 1m1½f Wolverhampton AW trip. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in style — Kaaranah, Beachborough Girl, Wolf Of Badenoch, Asian Journey, Implied Volatility, Le Pelerin and Have You A Minute are all true hold-up types, though several have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot physically accommodate that many horses at the rear. With Study Up able to control fractions unopposed, this race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or at least travel in the first half of the field, as a steady pace will compress the finish and give the leader a significant first-run advantage over those making ground from deep. The field holds far more hold-up horses than can realistically settle at the back, meaning Kaaranah, Beachborough Girl and Wolf Of Badenoch are among those most likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than their natural style dictates.

scenarios.body: If Study Up's rider misjudges, sets an extremely slow pace and the entire field concertinas approaching the home turn, producing a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Study Up (Jonny Peate) is the race-shaper — if he is allowed to stride clear unopposed in the first half-mile, the entire field is in a catch-me-if-you-can scenario and the race is effectively over early.

Kaaranah and Beachborough Girl are both natural hold-up horses who may be forced forward by the compressed field — watch their early positions at the start, as their jockeys' decisions in the first two furlongs will define which scenario unfolds.

Eagle Day's fading-in-finish flag combined with an uncontested front-runner ahead is a dangerous combination — Pat Cosgrave will need to time a move much earlier than usual or risk the horse emptying at the critical moment.

Implied Volatility (151 days) and Have You A Minute (197 days) are both returning from significant absences — monitor market moves for either horse as signs of home readiness, as their true chances are very hard to assess on form alone.

Wolf Of Badenoch's Standard going figures (0W0P from 4/15) are markedly poor and the 27-day break adds uncertainty — in a race with a pace-dominant shape that already limits hold-up types, his profile is doubly disadvantaged.
